Avoid - excretion in milk; insufficient data
Caution in severe impairment; limited data
HbA1c, blood glucose; QT in at-risk patients
summary: Teneligliptin is a DPP-4 inhibitor used for type 2 diabetes, marketed in Japan, India, and other countries but NOT FDA-approved. It uniquely does not require renal dose adjustment due to dual hepatic/renal elimination. Authored from SmPC/regional prescribing information and review literature - PENDING CLINICAL REVIEW; verify against local approved labeling before use.
indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, as monotherapy or in combination with diet and exercise or other antidiabetic agents (per regional approvals; not FDA-approved)

dosage.n: May increase to 40 mg once daily based on response

dosage.d: 20 mg once daily; no adjustment required

admin: Take once daily, with or without food
Can be taken at any consistent time of day
moa: Selectively and reversibly inhibits dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4), preventing degradation of the incretin hormones GLP-1 and GIP. This increases glucose-dependent insulin secretion and decreases glucagon, lowering blood glucose with low intrinsic hypoglycemia risk.

absolute: Severe infection, perioperative state, serious trauma (use insulin)

preg: Not recommended; safety in pregnancy has not been established. Use insulin to manage diabetes in pregnancy.
lact: Avoid; animal data show excretion into milk. Safety in breastfeeding not established.
renal: No dose adjustment required across renal impairment stages including end-stage renal disease, because teneligliptin undergoes both hepatic metabolism and renal excretion (dual elimination).
hepatic: Use with caution in moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment; data are limited. Mild impairment generally needs no adjustment.

major: Class IA/III antiarrhythmics and other QT-prolonging drugs (additive QT prolongation)
moderate: Sulfonylureas / insulin (increased hypoglycemia - consider dose reduction)
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excess - may increase hypoglycemia risk

monitoring: ECG/QT in patients with cardiac risk or on QT-prolonging drugs
counsel: Take once daily; continue diet and exercise
Report severe persistent abdominal pain (possible pancreatitis)
Know symptoms of low blood sugar, especially if also taking sulfonylurea or insulin
Note: this medicine is not FDA-approved - follow your local prescriber's guidance
pk: DPP-4 inhibition within hours; glycemic effect over days to weeks
Plasma peak ~1-2 hours after oral dose
Store at controlled room temperature; protect from moisture
pearls: No renal dose adjustment needed - useful in chronic kidney disease
Long half-life (~24 h) from anchor-domain binding to DPP-4
NOT approved by the US FDA; widely used in Japan, India, and parts of Asia/Latin America
Weight-neutral with low intrinsic hypoglycemia risk
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the schedule. Do not take two doses together.
overdose: Limited data. Overdose may increase risk of QT prolongation and hypoglycemia (especially with other agents). Management is supportive with glucose monitoring and ECG; dialysis is unlikely to substantially remove the drug.
